Static coverage of all 68 extracted files was complete, with two low-severity findings: remote whisper markup may spoof notification display (medium confidence), and persistent history has retention but no per-day size cap (high confidence). No high-risk exfiltration or code-execution path was found in this package. The publisher did not expose a checksum; this digest was computed from the official CDN download. BazCore, source-to-release equivalence, and runtime behavior were outside scope.
warnings: Requires BazCore, a separate addon; CurseForge says its app installs this dependency automatically, while manual users must install it separately.
Auto Loot is enabled by default and the addon sets the global WoW autoLootDefault CVar to 1. Default settings hide Blizzard’s loot window and loot popups.
Notification history stores titles, messages, icons, priorities and timestamps locally in SavedVariables for 7 days by default; users may configure 1–90 days and clear it.

Low-severity static finding: remote whisper formatting is passed to WoW notification text without markup neutralization. It may spoof or distort display; no code-execution path was found, and runtime rendering was not tested.
Low-severity static finding: retained notification history has no per-day entry or byte limit. Sustained events may enlarge local SavedVariables and slow history or persistence work.

The exact v032 ZIP passed a complete static scan with the two findings above. BazCore, in-game runtime/compatibility, and source-to-release equivalence were not tested. CurseForge published no checksum on the reviewed page; the displayed SHA-256 is our digest of the official CDN file.
